trust_decision.summary: Possession of a UniqueId 'name' value (sent in emailed links) is treated as authorization to accept/decline an event invitation or confirm a lead-capture opt-in; the value is minted in UniqueId repository getNew() via Util::generateMoreEntropyId(), which uses rand()/uniqid (not a CSPRNG).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'weak token generation via rand()'; grepping for rand() in the ID helpers leads straight to Util::generateMoreEntropyId (and its neighbours generateId/generateKey).

fix_sites.entry_point: Public static API Util::generateMoreEntropyId() (made to delegate to generateCryptId); reached by any caller including extensions

UniqueId repository getNew(), used by event invitation emails (application/Espo/Modules/Crm/Business/Event/Invitations.php:192) and lead-capture opt-in (application/Espo/Tools/LeadCapture/CaptureService.php:206); tokens consumed by entryPoint=eventConfirmation and entryPoint=confirmOptIn

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both producers of UniqueId funnel through one repository getNew() (EntityManager::getNewEntity -> getEntity -> getRepository()->getNew(), application/Espo/ORM/EntityManager.php:221-237); no second implementation of the UniqueId token was found.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Util::generateKey() (CSP nonce) and Util::generatePassword() (mt_rand) are separate helpers for 'a nonce' and 'a password', not the 'unique ID' tokens the report talks about; and generateId() is documented as a plain 17-char record ID, so a solver can say these are not covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Util::generateId() (uniqid + rand) is the default record-ID generator and a Formula function. Its 17-character, time-ordered format is relied on for entity IDs. Replacing it with a 32-hex crypt ID, or changing generateMoreEntropyId's length without widening the column, breaks ID format or storage. The fix adds maxLength 64 to UniqueId.name for this reason.

O7_producer.where: application/Espo/Repositories/UniqueId.php:43-50 (repository getNew sets the token); consumed by application/Espo/Modules/Crm/EntryPoints/EventConfirmation.php:87-91 and application/Espo/Tools/LeadCapture/CaptureService.php:430-434

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Generated user passwords (admin 'generate password', password send/reset, Formula password\generate, OIDC sync stub) come from Util::generatePassword, which picks and shuffles characters with mt_rand
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is password generation, not token/ID generation, and it uses mt_rand rather than the rand() the report names
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as landing point; callers in application/Espo/Tools/UserSecurity/Password/Generator.php:75, application/Espo/Services/User.php:100, application/Espo/Tools/UserSecurity/Password/Service.php:245,296, application/Espo/Core/Authentication/Oidc/UserProvider/Sync.php:68

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CSP script nonce for every rendered page is Util::generateKey() = md5(uniqid(rand(), true))
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A CSP nonce is a defence-in-depth header value, not an access token; it is per-response and not stored

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebSocket WAMP session ID uses uniqid(mt_rand())
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Separate optional transport (the WebSocket daemon); the session ID may not be an authorization secret

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Password-recovery requestId produced by a local helper based on uniqid/rand instead of Util::generateCryptId
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix commit is titled 'Better recovery unique ID', and older code used the same md5(uniqid(rand())) idiom as generateKey

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A LeadCapture formId (a public, unauthenticated form identifier) generated by Util::generateId, plus a token-like reuse of it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already uses the non-crypto generateId; a maintainer could plausibly treat the formId as a secret

services: MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL for the integration tests; unit tests need none
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/Espo/Core/Utils/UtilTest.php covers Util helpers; the fix adds no tests. A behavioural test of randomness quality is hard: it can only check format/length or mock the CSPRNG

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace rand() with random_int() inside generateMoreEntropyId only, still md5/truncated, or switch every Util::generate* (including record-ID generateId) to random_bytes and break ID format

out_of_scope_notes: application/Espo/Core/Mail/EmailSender.php:156 uses mt_rand in mail construction (likely boundary/message-id); not an authorization secret, not pursued.
application/Espo/Core/Select/Helpers/RandomStringGenerator.php:36 uses rand() for query aliases; not security relevant.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check performed).

Whether a behavioural hidden test can tell a CSPRNG from rand() in PHP (e.g. by seeding mt_srand/srand and checking that tokens are not predictable) was not evaluated; this testability concern may be the biggest practical risk.
